thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU autoscaler ceiling reached for pool 'inference-westus'. Queue length spiked to 920, requests being throttled. Autoscaler at max_nodes=50. Alert: high request latency and 429s.
Priya (sre-oncall): On it. Paging infra. Is this impacting hosted API customers or only Dedicated?
Mark (infra): Seeing it in metrics — both hosted and dedicated inference jobs routed to that pool. Autoscaler config: maxNodes: 50, scalePolicy: conservative. Pod pending backlog high, podCount==50, node utilization ~99%.
Anjali (eng-runtime): Noted. We have a bunch of long-context CRT jobs piling up from a single tenant (org-17). Could be hotspot. Any chance of KV cache saturation?
Tom (prod-ops): Confirming customer-facing 95p latency jumped to ~18s in the last 8m, and API is returning more 429s. Tagged top customers — org-17 + a few small teams.
Priya (sre-oncall): Can someone try a manual cap raise? We need immediate relief and then follow up with traffic shaping. Who owns the cloud quota bump?
Mark (infra): I can do an emergency bump but need cost approval for temporary capacity. Also need to confirm cluster pod limits. Running checks now.
Mark (infra): Quick checks: 
``` 
kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-westus -o wide
# nodes 50 Ready
kubectl get pvs | grep inference
# no obvious storage pressure
gcloud compute autoscaler describe inference-autoscaler --region=us-west1
# max: 50, policy: cpu-utilization 80%
``` 
Anjali (eng-runtime): We can also enable short-term request shedding for long sequences (max_tokens cap) for non-enterprise routes to reduce tokens in flight. But that's code change and slow. Manual node bump buys runway.
Dave (finance): What's the expected delta cost for bumping to 70 nodes for 2 hours? Need quick estimate before I sign off.
Mark (infra): Rough calc: +20 nodes * 8 GPUs/node * ~$3.2/hr per GPU ~= $512/hr -> ~$1024 for 2 hours. I can absorb on SRE incident budget, Dave.
Dave (finance): OK from finance side, prioritize customer uptime. :thumbsup:
Priya (sre-oncall): Mark, go ahead. Annotate with incident tag and expiration. Post the exact command output when done.
Mark (infra): Executing manual increase now. Running cloud console CLI: 
``` 
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize inference-pool-westus --region=us-west1 --size=70
# API accepts resize, operation started
``` 
deploy-bot: Resize operation started: operation-ops-1840005200 (status: RUNNING)
Mark (infra): Resize finished. Nodes 70 reporting as Ready. Reconfiguring autoscaler max_nodes -> 80 and setting a 3h cooldown. 
``` 
gcloud compute autoscaler update inference-autoscaler --region=us-west1 --max-num-replicas=80
# update OK
``` 
Mark (infra): Autoscaler updated, manual bump annotated: reason="emergency-queue-unblock" expires=2026-03-15T14:45Z
Priya (sre-oncall): Monitoring metrics — queue dropping, 429s down to baseline. Customers rerouting succeeded. Please keep an eye on org-17 tail behavior.
Anjali (eng-runtime): I triggered a temporary per-request token cap for public routes to limit worst offenders: `max_tokens=1024` for non-enterprise keys. Will roll back after stabilization.
Tom (prod-ops): Verified API error rate back to normal for most customers. Two small retries needed for org-17. No data loss reported.
Mark (infra): Manual action log: `resize->70`, `autoscaler.max->80`, cooldown 3h. Leaving monitoring alert escalations on.
Priya (sre-oncall): Handing off to Mark for 2h watch. I'll start an incident write-up. Assigning postmortem: owners Priya + Anjali, due EOD tomorrow. Action items: 1) investigate org-17 workload shaping, 2) revisit autoscaler policy and pod limits, 3) improve runbook for manual cap raise.
Dave (finance): Please add a billing note for emergency bump so I can code it to incident budget.
Mark (infra): Added annotation in billing tickets and incident log.
Priya (sre-oncall): Thanks team. Closing immediate paging loop. :white_check_mark: Will reopen if queue climbs again.
Priya (sre-oncall): Post-incident note: avoid permanent autoscaler increases without capacity planning. We'll schedule a dedicated capacity review with product for org-17 workload later this week."
